description:
FILED s463av from the #981 profile of the `slices` bench row, which is the row
that carries the shape: `my %h = map { $_ => $_ } 1..50; my @k = (1..10);` then
`@h{@k}` in a loop.  Every iteration stringifies the same ten integers again.

MEASURED (sb-sprof, N = 1.5e6, 1492 samples, on the s463av tree):

    %p-fixnum-string        4.8 % self / 7.6 % total
    to-string               0.7 %
    stringify-value         0.7 %
    ------------------------------------------------
    key stringification    ~9 % of the row

against ~21 % for the hash machinery itself (gethash/equal 20.6 % total, with
perhaps-truncated-equal-hash 4.7 %, %sxhash-string/truncating 1.5 %, string=*
2.3 % underneath it).

WHY IT IS NOT ALREADY CACHED, and this is the part worth writing down.  A PCL
box has an SV cache (`p-box-sv` / `p-box-sv-ok`) exactly so that a scalar used
as a hash key stringifies once — that is what #922's closing note meant by "the
residue is the box's SV cache".  But since the boxed-aggregates flip
(`docs/boxed-aggregates-design-s455.md`) an array ELEMENT holds a RAW value
until something takes an alias to it, so `@k`'s ten slots hold bare integers
with NO box and therefore NO SV cache.  The optimization that made element
reads cheap is the same one that removed the place the string half lived.  This
is a genuine trade, not a regression — a box per element costs more than the
stringify in every other row — but it means "raw element + numeric hash key" is
a shape with no cache anywhere.

THE OBVIOUS CANDIDATE, AND THE HAZARD THAT MUST BE ANSWERED FIRST: a
preallocated table of strings for small non-negative fixnums (0..1023, say),
returned by `%p-fixnum-string` instead of a fresh string.  It would remove
essentially all of the 9 % on this shape and help every `"$n"` and every
numeric hash key in the corpus.

The hazard is SHARING.  Today every call returns a FRESH simple-string, so a
caller may keep it, store it in a box, and let a later `.=` mutate it — PCL's
str-buffer optimization appends in place.  A shared table entry that some
program mutates would corrupt every other use of that number, everywhere, for
the life of the image: a silent-wrong of the worst kind.  So the measurement to
take FIRST is not the speedup, it is: does any path store the result of
`%p-fixnum-string` somewhere that can later be mutated in place?  Audit
`to-string` / `stringify-value` / `box-sv` / the str-buffer promotion, and if
any can, the table is only safe behind a copy-on-promote or a read-only marker
— at which point re-measure, because the copy may cost what the table saves.

DO NOT ship the table without that audit.

SHIPPED s464ax (round 22 PERF slot, 2026-09-02), on top of #985 (`0e54656`).
The table IS worth it, and by a lot more than this task estimated.

THE HAZARD THE TASK SAID TO ANSWER FIRST, ANSWERED TWO WAYS.

(a) AUDIT.  Every in-place string writer in `cl/` was read.  Not one writes
into a string it did not make: `magical-string-increment` COPY-SEQs first;
`p-chop-single` / `p-chomp-single` build with SUBSEQ; `p-vec-set` takes
COPY-SEQ or CONCATENATE; `p-string-bit-op` makes a fresh MAKE-STRING;
`%pcl-str-buffer` (the str-buffer store discipline) allocates a fresh
adjustable buffer and REPLACEs into it; `%pcl-str-append` extends its OWN
accumulator and only READS the source; `%psos-put` goes through `%psos-buf`,
which rebuilds unless the box already holds an ADJUSTABLE fill-pointer string
â a table entry is a simple-string, so it rebuilds; the XS bridge takes
STRING-TO-OCTETS (a fresh octet vector) before any SAP.  `p-box-sv` caches a
string but only ever REPLACES it wholesale.

(b) MEASURED, which is the half that matters.  A 16-route probe was written
for the ways a `to-string` RESULT (the entry itself, not a copy) reaches a
scalar the program can write to: a hash KEY handed back by `keys` / `each` /
a foreach over `keys`, interpolation of a lone value, `join`, `sprintf "%s"`,
an array element, then chop / substr-lvalue / vec-lvalue / an in-memory
filehandle / `++` / `s///` / `tr///` / a str-buffer accumulator applied to
each.  Two runs:

  * with the table entries deliberately built ADJUSTABLE with a fill-pointer
    â i.e. mutable in place, the worst case the hazard describes â ALL 16
    routes still read correctly;
  * with entry 5 POISONED to "ZZ", the first field reads `key:ZZ`, which
    proves the probe reaches the table at all (without this the "nothing
    corrupted" result would have been vacuous).

Both are guard rows now, with the poison/adjustable results recorded beside
them.  Standing rule written into the runtime comment: a future in-place
string writer MUST copy first.

THE CHANGE.  Today's digit loop is renamed `%p-fixnum-string-digits` and is
untouched.  `*p-small-fixnum-strings*` is 1024 entries (~32 KB) BUILT BY that
loop, so the text is identical by construction rather than by a second
implementation.  `%p-fixnum-string` is now an inline dispatcher: `(typep n
'(integer 0 1023))` -> `svref`, else the loop.  `stringify-value` is NOT
touched (its float/box/overload arms are untouched â the sibling agent s464aw
owns those this round).

MEASURED.  The bench tool's own noise on this box was 8-15 % on `slices` while
a sibling agent ran, so the primary instrument is an interleaved wall-time A/B
of the two SAVED CORES on one emitted program, startup subtracted, best-of-K,
with a same-core CONTROL run alternately:

    program            control (A vs A)     A/B (A=table, B=0e54656)
    slices, N=1.5e6    +1.6 % +0.7 %        +20.6 % +16.9 % +17.4 %
                       (B vs B) +0.2 %
    numstr-small       -0.8 %               +20.7 %      ("" . ($i % 1000), 4e6)
    numstr-big         +2.9 %               +0.1 %       ("" . ($i + 1e6), 4e6)
    numstr-neg         -0.6 %               +0.4 %       ("" . -$i, 4e6)

So: **~15 % of the `slices` program and ~17 % of a small-integer stringify
loop; the non-table paths (values > 1023, negatives) are unchanged** â the
extra TYPEP costs nothing measurable.

Interleaved sb-sprof of the same two cores, three rounds each, same load:

    A (table)     1472 / 1500 / 1480 samples   0.736 / 0.750 / 0.740 s CPU
    B (no table)  1754 / 1761 / 1737           0.877 / 0.881 / 0.869 s CPU

`%p-fixnum-string` is 5.5 / 5.1 / 4.5 % self in B and ABSENT from A (folded
into `stringify-value`'s 1.7-2.1 %).  Note the profile's own attribution
(6.5 % total) UNDERSTATES the win: the 15 M short-lived strings the digit loop
allocated cost more than the time inside it.

Whole board, `bench-exec.pl` A/B twice against `0e54656` with one CONTROL run:
`slices` **+13.5 % and +13.4 %** (base slower) in both; every other row
sign-mixed across the two runs and inside the control band (which on that
loaded box was Â±7 % on `intloop+=` and Â±33 % on `pack`).  `slices` reads
**2.49x / 2.51x** against Â§0.2f's 3.02x â with #985 that is 3.02x -> ~2.5x on
the round.

KEY TEXT.  48 numeric values (fixnum boundaries, the table boundary
1021..1025, negatives, floats, numeric strings, `0 but true`, `-0`, `1e3`)
printed AND used as hash keys, before and after: byte-identical, and identical
to perl 5.40.3 on all but ONE row, which is PRE-EXISTING and filed as **#1012**
(a float of magnitude exactly 1e15 prints as its integer text; perl says
`1e+15` â `stringify-value`'s float arm derives the exponent from a LOG that
lands on 14.999999999999998).

LEGS.  Paren check balanced; gate 193 files / 6544 rows (only the 13 pclxs xs
rows); full sweep TOTAL 18346 (+0) GATE clean, drops 5 = census; companion
`--all --quick`.  Runtime-only: emission unchanged, no generation bump, no
artifact regeneration.  Guards: `Pl/t/misc-fixes-02.t` 124 -> 126.

NOT DONE, with the reason: the range is 0..1023 and was not tuned.  4096
entries would cost 128 KB and cover more loop counters, but the measured win
is already the allocation, not the digit count, and no corpus measurement was
taken to justify a bigger table.  NEGATIVE small values are also not tabled
(`-1` is common) â same reason.  If someone revisits, the instrument is
`wallab.pl` in the session scratchpad (interleaved wall-time A/B of two saved
cores on one emitted program): it resolves 1 % where `bench-exec` on a shared
box resolves 15 %.


=== FABLE REVIEW + MERGE (s464, 2026-09-02) === diff read; probes vs perl 5.40.3 on both PCL_OPT paths (ovl.pl 37 rows for #972/#987: 33 identical, the 4 diffs are the declined #960(a) refusal); rebased and merged ff into main (round 22: AW 3d666ea, AX 300d47f); legs on the final tree in DECIDED s464 round-22 record.
subject: Perf: a numeric hash key read from an ARRAY re-stringifies on every use — raw element storage left no SV to cache the string half in (%p-fixnum-string is 7.6 % of the `slices` row)
